# Market data test fixtures

`futures-reference.json` is a recorded response from Finviz's public `api/futures_all?timeframe=i5` endpoint, retrieved on 2026-10-11 UTC (2026-10-10 New York). It contains 59 actual reference instruments; sparklines retain the final 60 source samples and sparse chart labels are omitted. It is a regression fixture, never a runtime market source or a current quote reference.

Browser checks deliberately stub desktop IPC with this recorded response to verify filtering, precision, source labeling, and cached failures. A separate live source probe verified the actual endpoint and schemas. Native tests also use controlled invalid and boundary inputs to reproduce failure cases.

`finviz-overview-2026.html` is a complete saved Finviz screener page: the first 20 of 899 results (`#1 / 899 Total`) of a filtered stock screen in the Overview view (`v=111`), with its scripts, inline styles and inline event handlers. It moved here in 2.0.0. `tests/finviz.test.js` parses it as a whole page (its 20 symbols and the result count), `tests/inertHtml.test.js` checks the inline-handler stripping against it, and `scripts/verify-alerts.mjs` serves it as the Overview's first page when it tabs through the rows.

`finviz-overview-grid-2026-10-17.html` and `finviz-overview-grid-2026-10-21.html` are the live `screener.ashx?v=111&o=change` ARIA grid, trimmed to the header row and two quote rows (scripts, styles and icons removed, markup otherwise untouched). The 10-21 capture is the one where header cells gained an `aria-label`, a short-label span and a sort indicator, and ticker cells gained `data-ticker`. `node scripts/verify-finviz-live.mjs` checks the live views against the parser whenever Finviz is suspected to have changed again.

`finviz-overview-grid-2026-10-31-r21.html`, `finviz-etf-grid-141-2026-10-31.html` and `finviz-etf-grid-161-2026-10-31.html` are the live grids of `https://finviz.com/screener/stocks?v=111&o=change&r=21`, `https://finviz.com/screener/etf?v=141&f=etf_sectype_exchangetradedfund&o=-perf4w` and `https://finviz.com/screener/etf?v=161&f=etf_sectype_exchangetradedfund&o=-dividendyield`, retrieved on 2026-10-31 UTC. Each keeps its result count line (`#21 / 5620 Total` in the overview grid, `#1 / 5832 Total` in the ETF grids), the grid element with its `aria-rowcount`, the header row and the first three (overview) or two (ETF) quote rows; style attributes, logo images and icons were removed and the markup is otherwise untouched. They carry the `data-column-id` and `data-ticker` attributes the parser binds by, and the row numbers and counts it pages by.

`finviz-quote-AAPL-2026-10-31.html` is the live `https://finviz.com/stock?t=AAPL&p=d` (200, no redirect), the stock page's quote URL, retrieved on 2026-10-31 at 05:38 UTC. It is trimmed to the snapshot tables and the first 31 headlines; scripts, styles, ad slots and inline event handlers were removed and the kept markup is unchanged, as a comment at the top of the file records. `tests/finvizQuote.test.js` runs the quote-page parser (`src/utils/finvizQuote.js`) against it: the statistics, the `52W High` and `52W Low` bounds the 52-week strip reads, and the publisher Finviz names for each headline.

`yahoo-chart-AAPL-1mo-2026-10-30.json` and `yahoo-chart-PLUG-1mo-2026-10-30.json` are verbatim Yahoo v8 chart responses (`range=1mo&interval=1d`), recorded with curl at the app's URL on 2026-10-31 at 05:32 UTC, after the 2026-10-30 session. AAPL is a Nasdaq Global Select listing; PLUG is a sub-$5 Nasdaq Capital Market listing whose last daily close (1.37) differs from its `regularMarketPrice` (1.365). Neither response carries `exchangeDataDelayedBy` or `previousClose`: Yahoo's chart endpoint states no delay, which is why technical alerts judge a quote by its own age. `tests/marketData.test.js` and `scripts/verify-native-marketdata.mjs` read them, and the browser checks serve them to the stock page.

`futures-i5-2026-10-31.json` holds five records (ES, NCF, TIO, UX and ZK) copied verbatim from one live `https://finviz.com/api/futures_all?timeframe=i5` response retrieved on 2026-10-31 at 05:32:57 UTC; its `source`, `retrievedAt` and `note` fields say so. The 5-minute series of TIO, UX and ZK end away from their quotes, NCF's spans months but ends at its quote, and ES's is an ordinary one. `tests/futures.test.js` and `scripts/verify-native-futures.mjs` use them to check the rule that hides a sparkline whose samples do not agree with the quote.

The browser regressions' own recordings (the Overview's first losers page and two Yahoo charts that the alert checks score, one of which they also reuse with test-only closes) live in `ui/` and are described in [`ui/README.md`](ui/README.md).
